feedback: For a wrong match, give a conditions hint: 'a cactus needs dry, sunny conditions — would a wet pond suit it?'
If a child sorts by size of animal rather than scale of place, re-focus on the place: is this the whole surrounding area, or a small spot within a larger one?
activities.intendedInsight: Not every living thing can live in any place; a match is justified by the conditions a place offers and what the plant or animal is adapted to. The habitat/microhabitat sort reinforces the two scales.
learnerActions: Match living-thing cards (animals and plants) to habitat scenes (cactus, a plant→desert; crab→rock pool; fox→woodland; frog→pond).
For each match, add a 'why?' using 'conditions', 'adapted to' or 'shelter' (e.g. 'a cactus is adapted to dry, sunny conditions').
Test a deliberately wrong pairing (cactus→pond) and explain why the conditions do not suit it.
Sort a second set of cards into 'whole habitat' vs 'microhabitat inside it'.
activities.title: Match animals to habitats and justify with conditions

feedback: If 'habitat' and 'microhabitat' are used interchangeably, make the nesting physical: point from the crack (microhabitat) out to the whole pool (habitat).

If 'conditions' means only 'the weather', scaffold with a frame — 'The conditions in a rock pool are ___ and ___' — to attach it to wet, salty, cold. Treat this as a word that needs exercise, not a misconception.
For the bird's nest question, accept that a nest is most precisely the bird's shelter, not the whole habitat; use it to re-separate shelter from the surrounding place.
Encourage transfer: ask the child to describe a second, contrasting habitat using the same words.
activities.intendedInsight: Meaning is shown by correct USE in running description — naming the whole place as the habitat/environment, a crevice as a microhabitat within it, the specific conditions (wet, salty, cold, pounding waves), and the animal's shelter — not by reciting definitions.
learnerActions: Look at a rock pool or woodland picture.
Describe the place aloud: where a crab (or other animal) lives, what it is like there, and where it can hide.
Use whichever words fit while narrating: habitat, microhabitat, conditions, shelter, environment.

Answer follow-up prompts: point to a microhabitat inside the habitat; name the conditions that make a rock pool hard to live in; use 'environment' in a sentence about the seashore; decide whether a bird's nest is a habitat, a microhabitat or just a shelter, and why.
activities.title: Describe a habitat aloud using the target words

feedback: If the child names only the shelter, ask for the whole surrounding place too.
Prompt for at least one named condition before moving on.
activities.intendedInsight: The same vocabulary can be rehearsed through dialogue, prompting a child to supply habitat, conditions and shelter for a described animal.
learnerActions: Listen to or read an animal persona describing where it lives and asking 'where do I live, and why does it suit me?'
Name the animal's habitat and the conditions it needs.
Point out a microhabitat within the habitat where the animal might find shelter, and say how the microhabitat and the shelter differ from the whole habitat.
activities.title: Meet an animal who describes its home
